## Claims
- [source-backed] \(I_{r,q}=\operatorname{Span}_{\mathbb Z}\{s_\lambda:\lambda\nsubseteq q^r\}\), and \(\Lambda/I_{r,q}\) has Schur classes indexed by \(\lambda\subseteq q^r\). [doi:10.1112/jlms.12832, lines 213-218]
- [source-backed] For \(v_{r,s,t,n}\), \(i=s-t+1\), \(j=r-t+1\), and \(a=\min(n-r-i,r-j)\), \(b=\min(i,j)\); the lower family is indexed by \(i^j\subseteq\mu\subseteq(i^j,b^a)\). [doi:10.1112/jlms.12832, lines 219-235]
- [source-backed] Partition conjugation is a ring involution and sends \(I_{r,n-r}\) to \(I_{n-r,r}\). [source-2, lines 1756-1772]
- [proved] Under \(r=j+c,\ q=i+p,\ i,j\ge1,\ p,c\ge0\), conjugation induces \(\Lambda/I_{q,r}\cong\Lambda/I_{r,q}\), transports the interval ideal and \(A_+J\), and sends the lower family for \((q,r,j,i,c,p)\) bijectively onto the right family for \((r,q,i,j,p,c)\).

## Strategy
Put \(A_{r,q}=\Lambda/I_{r,q}\), and define
\[
J_{r,q}^{i,j}:=\bigoplus_{i^j\subseteq\lambda\subseteq q^r}\mathbb Z\bar s_\lambda\subseteq A_{r,q}.
\]
This is an ideal: in every nonzero Littlewood--Richardson term of
\(\bar s_\lambda\bar s_\theta\), the resulting partition contains \(\lambda\); hence it still contains \(i^j\).

Since
\[
\lambda\nsubseteq r^q\iff\lambda'\nsubseteq q^r,
\]
\(\omega(I_{q,r})=I_{r,q}\). Thus
\[
\bar\omega:A_{q,r}\xrightarrow{\sim}A_{r,q},\qquad
\bar s_\lambda\longmapsto\bar s_{\lambda'}
\]
is an integral graded ring isomorphism. Moreover,
\[
i^j\subseteq\lambda\subseteq r^q
\iff
j^i\subseteq\lambda'\subseteq q^r,
\]
so
\[
\bar\omega(J_{q,r}^{j,i})=J_{r,q}^{i,j}.
\]
Grading gives \(\bar\omega((A_{q,r})_+)=(A_{r,q})_+\); therefore
\[
\bar\omega\!\left((A_{q,r})_+J_{q,r}^{j,i}\right)
=(A_{r,q})_+J_{r,q}^{i,j}.
\]

Let \(a=\min(p,c)\), \(b=\min(i,j)\). The lower-adjoined family in the domain is
\[
\mathcal L_{q,r}^{j,i}
=\{\bar s_{(j^i,\rho)}:\rho\subseteq b^a\}.
\]
For \(\rho\subseteq b^a\),
\[
(j^i,\rho)'=
\bigl(i+\rho'_1,\ldots,i+\rho'_b,i^{\,j-b}\bigr).
\]
As \(\rho\mapsto\rho'\) bijects partitions in \(b^a\) with those in \(a^b\), this yields exactly
\[
\bar\omega(\mathcal L_{q,r}^{j,i})
=
\left\{\bar s_\mu:
i^j\subseteq\mu\subseteq((i+a)^b,i^{\,j-b})\right\},
\]
the right-adjoined family for \((r,q,i,j,p,c)\). The box conditions hold because
\[
a\le p=q-i,\qquad a\le c=r-j.
\]

For admissibility, the original tuple corresponds to
\[
n=r+q,\qquad s=i+c,\qquad t=c+1.
\]
Then
\[
1\le t\le r,s\le n,\qquad
r+s-n=c-p<t=c+1.
\]
After interchange,
\[
r^\vee=q,\quad s^\vee=j+p,\quad t^\vee=p+1,
\]
and
\[
1\le t^\vee\le r^\vee,s^\vee\le n,\qquad
r^\vee+s^\vee-n=p-c<t^\vee=p+1.
\]
Finally,
\[
i^\vee=s^\vee-t^\vee+1=j,\quad
j^\vee=r^\vee-t^\vee+1=i,\quad
p^\vee=c,\quad c^\vee=p.
\]
Hence the transformed parameter tuple is precisely \((q,r,j,i,c,p)\).

The requested parameter-conjugation certificate is established.

## Gaps
None for this algebraic certificate. It does not itself assert minimality of either family.
